strategies.name: Zero-Bot & Tetraphobia Shield
strategies.description: Dual anti-crowd arbitrage. Bans the bot-consensus leaders (08, 22, 30, 32, 46, 48) and every digit-8 ball, locks the six zero-bot-pick balls' tetraphobia tier (13, 20, 34, 40), and fills from uncrowded >31 tetraphobia and prime anchors so the line clears 186.
rules: Ban the bot-consensus leaders 08, 22, 30, 32, 46, 48 and every digit-8 ball.
Always carry the zero-bot-pick pool 13, 20, 34, 40 — 34 and 40 are tetraphobia above 31.
Fill two more slots from 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 47, 49 so the sum lands in 186–205.
strategies.math: In a pari-mutuel game the expected return falls with the number of co-winners, so a line is maximised by avoiding both human superstition and algorithmic consensus at once.

strategies.name: Mod-9 Residue Equilibrium & Digital Root 7
strategies.description: Exploits the one structural anomaly the randomness audit flags. Splits the line across six distinct mod-9 residue classes with at least three of them from the six-ball classes, and locks the sum to digital root 7 — 160, 169, 178 or 187.
rules: Six balls from six different mod-9 residue classes, at least three from the six-ball classes.
The residue classes must sum to 7 (mod 9).
The line sum must be exactly 160, 169, 178 or 187.
strategies.math: Every other sum rule treats 177, 178 and 179 as equivalent; only a residue-locked line rides the single chi-square failure in 1,238 draws.

strategies.name: 50-Draw Velocity & 50-n Mirror Twin
strategies.description: Anchors the line on the strongest short-term velocity leaders when they happen to form a 50-n mirror pair, vetoes the five fastest-falling balls, and tops up with the remaining risers and the >31 payout anchors.
rules: Take the velocity leaders of the last 50 draws; when two of them sum to 50, that pair is the core.
Veto the five balls with the most negative 50-draw residual.
Fill the rest from the remaining risers and the anchors 41 and 47.
strategies.math: All-time frequencies decay badly inside a cold regime; a short-window residual plus a mirror pair buys momentum and symmetry in two slots.

strategies.name: Lag-1 Kinetic Carryover & 7th-Ball Bridge
strategies.description: Anti-gambler's-fallacy engine. Spends one slot on the previous draw's additional (7th) ball, one on a ±1 neighbour of a previous main ball, and fills the rest inside the observed 20-draw gap window — balls overdue by more than 20 draws are rejected outright.
rules: Slot 1: the previous draw's additional ball, else its highest main number.
Slot 2: a ±1 neighbour of one of the previous draw's six main balls.
Slots 3–6: balls seen within the last 20 draws; reject any ball overdue by more.
strategies.math: 58% of draws contain a lag-1 repeater and 12.6% promote the 7th ball; the line is shaped to meet that density instead of fighting it.

strategies.name: Second-Order Z-Score Graph Filtering
strategies.description: Builds the line as a six-vertex graph. The anchor is the pair with the strongest standardised co-occurrence residual, the documented repulsion and drought pairs are vetoed outright, and at most two of the fifteen edges may fall below the expected co-occurrence.
strategies.edge: Second-order graph harmony, no dead edges
rules: Anchor the strongest positive pair from the 49×49 co-occurrence matrix.
Keep at most two of the fifteen pairs below the expected co-occurrence.
strategies.math: Combining individually strong numbers without a second-order check plants a dead edge inside the ticket; the clique sieve removes it.

strategies.name: Asymmetric Composition Cell & High-AC Sieve
strategies.description: Plays the composition matrix's strongest cell instead of the recommended symmetric split: three odd and three even, exactly two balls above 24, at least three of the four low balls in the upper-low band 19–24, Arithmetic Complexity of at least 9, no consecutive pair and no three-term progression.
strategies.edge: #1 matrix cell plus maximum gap dispersion
rules: Exactly 3 odd and 3 even balls, exactly 2 of them above 24.
At least 3 of the 4 low balls inside 19–24.
Arithmetic Complexity ≥ 9, no consecutive pair, no three-term progression.
strategies.math: Human players over-use arithmetic progressions and runs; a high-AC line keeps almost every pairwise gap unique.

strategies.name: Calendar-Conditional Regime Switching
strategies.description: Switches its core on the draw calendar. Monday draws anchor on the balls that skew Monday (18, 23, 39) with 40 excluded; Thursday draws anchor on 4, 20 and 46. The target sum drifts with the season — higher in the first quarter, lower mid-year.
rules: Monday draws: carry 18, 23 and 39, and exclude 40.
Thursday draws: carry 4, 20 and 46.
Target sum 155–190 in the first quarter, 142–172 in June, 145–185 otherwise.
strategies.math: A static ticket ignores a schedule-conditioned distribution; the weekday split alone spans nearly 9.2% between peak and trough.

strategies.name: Cascade Draw 4 Barbell & Span-43 Lock
strategies.description: A barbell built for cascade draws: one low anchor, five balls at 33 or above, nothing at all between 7 and 32. The span is pinned to the modal 42–44 and the sum to the 190+ band where Group 3 prizes peak.
rules: Smallest ball 04, 05 or 06; largest ball 47, 48 or 49; span 42–44.
No ball between 07 and 32 — the four middle balls sit in 33–46.
Line sum inside 190–215.
strategies.math: During a cascade frenzy the calendar zone floods; a barbell keeps the jackpot share thin while still riding the 43-mode span.

strategies.name: 5-Tail Terminal Digit Architecture
strategies.description: Matches the modal five-ending shape: six balls carrying exactly five distinct last digits, with the single repeated tail sitting in the strongest tail class (2) or the tetraphobia tail (4), at most one ball ending in 0 and a 1-1-1-2-1 decade spread.
rules: Exactly five distinct last digits — one homologous pair.
The repeated tail is 2 or 4; at most one ball ends in 0.
Decade spread 1-1-1-2-1 across the five decades.
strategies.math: Players either repeat too many endings or force six different ones; the five-ending mode is what the draw actually produces.

strategies.name: 7×7 Playslip Anti-Geometry & Cross-Corner
strategies.description: Harvests the cage geometry without the retail geometry. Two cells from playslip column 4, one high corner, and three balls off both main diagonals — with no row and no column holding more than two marks.
strategies.edge: Captures the 160.8% cross rate and avoids the slashes
rules: Two balls from playslip column 4 (04, 11, 18, 32, 39, 46), never row 4.
One high corner, 43 or 49.
The other three balls off both main diagonals; no row or column over two marks.
strategies.math: The centre cross and the corners hit above chance while the diagonals underperform — and diagonals are exactly where retail tickets cluster.
